newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up in deferreds on delayed seeding.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up in deferreds on delayed seeding.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures closed mostly higher, led by deferred months, with support stemming from concerns about delays in seeding portions of the U.S. soft red winter wheat crop, traders said.
Cash dealers early Friday indicated the eastern U.S. growing region would be slow in seeding the wheat crop due to the late harvest of soybeans.
"You can build a case for that but I think it's a little early to get carried away with it," one trader noted.

The late maturation of the soybean crop in the U.S. eastern Corn Belt led to the talk. A significant portion of wheat in that area is grown on land also used for soybeans. The U.S. soybean crop in some areas was planted late this year because of a wet spring seeding season.
USDA Monday confirmed the wheat seeding pace in Ohio, Indiana and Illinois were well behind the year-ago and average pace for this time of year.
Some traders also said the market was boosted by delays in harvesting of the Canadian spring wheat crop.
Wheat closed 5-1/4 cents a bushel higher to 1-1/2 lower, with December down 1-1/2 at $4.27.
Farmers Commodities Corp bought 1.5 million bushels of July and Merrill Lynch Futures bought one million December, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 12,000 contracts, down from 12,562 Tuesday, according to the CBOT.
In wheat options Prudential Securities bought 400 December $6.00 calls at 1/8 cent, Smith Barney sold 200 March $4.40 calls at 10 cents and sold 200 March $4.30 calls at 13 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 3,200 contracts, up from 2,513 Tuesday.
